before.title: AdBlue/SCR System Failure on BlueHDi Diesels — Urea Fault With Start-Prevention Countdown
before.description: BlueHDi diesel 208s suffer chronic AdBlue (SCR) system failures: the urea injection pump and its control electronics are integrated into the AdBlue tank, and pump seizure, urea crystallisation, faulty level sensors and (on pre-2018 cars) a non-vented filler cap that pulls a vacuum in the tank all kill urea delivery. The ECU then logs faults such as P20E8 (reductant pressure too low) or P20EE, lights the UREA/engine warning and starts a countdown (typically 1,100 km) after which the engine is prevented from starting. Peugeot's official fix is a complete new AdBlue tank assembly with ECU coding, quoted around GBP 1,100-1,300 at UK dealers.
before.solution: Diagnose which SCR component failed — NOx sensors and the AdBlue injector should be checked first, but a dead in-tank pump means a replacement AdBlue tank assembly that must be coded and primed to the car. Independent specialists and aftermarket repair kits can substantially undercut dealer pricing; do not ignore the countdown, as the car will refuse to restart at zero.
symptoms: UREA or AdBlue warning light with 'Engine fault: Repair needed' message
Start-prevention countdown in km shown on the dash
AdBlue level reads empty or incorrect despite being filled
Engine refuses to start once the countdown reaches zero
Repeated NOx sensor or anti-pollution faults that return after replacement

before.title: e-208 Battery Recalls — Fire Risk and Sudden Loss of Drive
before.description: The electric e-208 has been subject to several EU safety recalls for its battery systems. Cars built 15 January to 20 June 2020 were recalled (Peugeot code KQJ) because a manufacturing error in the 12V battery under the bonnet can short-circuit and cause a fire while charging or driving. Separately, faulty battery control-unit software on 2022-2023 cars (recall MV4, RAPEX alert 16/2025, 23,704 vehicles; plus a 21,349-vehicle KBA-listed campaign) can make 'Ready' mode unavailable and cut propulsion without warning while driving; an AC-compressor wiring fault (recall MF9, Oct 2019-Nov 2022 builds) could also shut down the powertrain.
before.solution: All fixes are free dealer recall work: battery replacement/inspection for the 2020 fire-risk campaign and software updates for the battery control unit and AC compressor logic. Owners should run their VIN through Peugeot's recall checker and confirm campaigns KQJ, MF9 and MV4 have been completed.
symptoms: Sudden loss of acceleration or drive power while moving
'Ready' mode unavailable after start-up
Powertrain shuts down with electrical fault warning
Burning smell or overheating around the under-bonnet 12V battery (fire-risk batch)
Recall letter or open campaign shown against the VIN

before.title: e-208 Onboard Charger (OBC) Failure — AC Charging Stops Working
before.description: The Mahle-manufactured 11 kW three-phase onboard charger (CAOBC1) fitted to e-208s built between 2019 and 2023 is prone to premature failure, often beginning around 10,000-12,000 miles. Failing units first charge erratically or drop from 11 kW three-phase to ~7 kW, then stop AC charging entirely, leaving only DC rapid charging usable. The replacement unit must be dealer-coded to the vehicle, and a new OBC costs roughly EUR 2,200-3,800 at a dealer.
before.solution: Stellantis extended the OBC warranty to 4 years (from April 2021) and replaces failed Mahle units with a more reliable VMAX charger; outside warranty, a dealer-fitted new OBC or a cheaper remanufactured unit (e.g. ACtronics) is the fix. Owners with intermittent charging should have the OBC checked before the failure becomes total.
symptoms: Car intermittently refuses to charge on AC wallbox or granny cable
Charging speed drops from 11 kW to about 7 kW on three-phase
'Charging impossible' or charge-fault message on dash
DC rapid charging still works while AC charging does not
Unpredictable charge sessions stopping after a few minutes

before.title: EAT6/EAT8 Automatic Gearbox Jerky Shifting and Low-Speed Hesitation
before.description: The Aisin-based EAT6 (late 208 I) and EAT8 (208 II) torque-converter automatics generate widespread owner complaints about jerky or harsh shifts at low speed, lag and flaring in 2nd gear, hesitation when accelerating from 2,000-3,000 rpm, and jerking on light-throttle deceleration in traffic. The behaviour stems from aggressive fuel-saving shift calibration and torque-management software, made worse by ageing transmission fluid; in a minority of cases valve-body or clutch-pack wear is involved. It is consistently reported across Peugeot Forums, the 208 Owners Club and UK gearbox specialists rather than being isolated complaints.
before.solution: A dealer TCU software update and adaptation reset resolves most low-speed jerkiness, and a transmission fluid service helps on higher-mileage cars even though Peugeot calls the box sealed-for-life. Persistent flaring or slipping needs a gearbox specialist to inspect the valve body and clutches.
symptoms: Jerky or harsh gear changes at low speed, especially 1st-3rd
Lag or flare when 2nd gear engages
Hesitant acceleration between 2,000-3,000 rpm
Jerking when decelerating slowly in traffic
Shifts smoother once the gearbox is warm

before.title: Front Suspension Knocking — Drop Links, Anti-Roll Bar Bushes and Damper Knock
before.description: First-generation 208s commonly develop knocking, clunking or rattling from the front suspension over bumps and rough surfaces. The usual culprits are worn ball-joint-type anti-roll bar drop links and perished ARB bushes, but 'damper knock' from the front struts and worn top mounts is also a well-known trait of the shared 208/2008/308 (T9) front suspension, which is why some owners replace drop links and still hear the noise. The noise is mainly an annoyance, but badly worn links and bushes degrade handling and will eventually fail an MOT.
before.solution: Inspect and replace worn drop links and anti-roll bar bushes first — a cheap job at any independent garage. If the knock persists, check strut top mounts and the dampers themselves, as 208 damper knock often requires new front shock absorbers.
symptoms: Knocking or clunking from the front over bumps and potholes
Rattling from one side of the front suspension on rough roads
Creaking or squeaking when the body rolls or over speed bumps
Noise persists after drop links have been replaced (damper/top-mount knock)
Vague or rattly feel through the steering on broken surfaces

before.title: PureTech 1.2 Wet Timing Belt Delamination
before.description: The 208's PSA/Stellantis PureTech 1.2 (EB2) engine uses an oil-immersed ("wet") timing belt rather than a chain. The belt's outer rubber layer can delaminate over time, shedding particles into the oil that clog the pickup strainer and starve the engine of oil. Stellantis revised the belt material and shortened service intervals (now 60,000 mi or 6 years), but earlier-spec belts remain at risk. Often appears first as a rattle at startup followed by oil pressure warnings.
before.solution: Replace the timing chain, tensioner, and sprockets with the updated revision parts. PSA extended the warranty to 10 years/200,000km for this specific issue on affected production dates.
symptoms: Engine rattle on startup
Check engine light
Loss of power
Engine misfires

proposal.title: PureTech 1.2 Wet Timing Belt Delamination

Its published terms cover affected 1.0/1.2 non-turbo engines produced June 2012-June 2022 and 1.2 turbo engines produced April 2014-June 2022. The 208 uses a belt, not the timing chain incorrectly named in the frozen solution, and the frozen 150-owner count has no traceable dataset.
proposal.solution: If an oil-pressure warning appears, stop the engine as soon as it is safe and do not continue driving until the lubrication system is checked. Identify the exact PureTech engine and production date by VIN; inspect belt condition using the current Peugeot procedure and, when degradation is confirmed, follow engine-specific instructions for the timing-belt system, oil pickup/lubrication circuit, oil and filter. Check Peugeot support eligibility and the vehicle service schedule. Do not buy a timing-belt kit from this page; production date, engine, diagnosis and VIN fitment must be established first.
